title: Dinosaurs: Evidence and Inference
subject: Reading
learning_objective: Use details and examples from a text to support inferences about characters or events.
instructions: Read independently. Use evidence from the passage to explain inferences. Compare details before choosing an answer.

story_content.opening: Two fossil sites told conflicting stories, and Dottie the Dino asked the explorers to decide which clues were stronger—and why.
story_content.passage: Site A contains crushed eggshells mixed with adult footprints facing outward, as if a caretaker left in a hurry. Site B shows intact nest circles but no adult tracks nearby. Explorers might infer Site A records a disturbed nest while Site B shows eggs left unattended. Dottie cautions that wind can erase tracks, so missing prints at Site B are weaker evidence than the outward tracks at Site A. Comparing both sites, the stronger claim is that Site A captures a moment of interruption. Any conclusion still needs more measurements of shell thickness and soil layers.
story_content.ending: Great work exploring dinosaurs ideas today!

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What can you reasonably infer from the passage?
choices: Site A more clearly shows a nest interruption than Site B
Nothing in the passage can be compared
A single photo proved every claim instantly
correct_answers: Site A more clearly shows a nest interruption than Site B
questions.explanation: The inference is supported by specific textual evidence.
hints: Combine two details rather than guessing.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Which evidence best supports the stronger claim in the passage?
choices: Adult footprints at Site A face outward as if leaving in a hurry
The teams skipped writing any logs
An unrelated sports score decided the case
correct_answers: Adult footprints at Site A face outward as if leaving in a hurry
questions.explanation: That detail is cited as the stronger support.
hints: Look for what the character treats as stronger evidence.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: Why does the passage reject a competing explanation?
choices: Missing prints at Site B are weaker because wind can erase tracks
Because the author said so without reasons
Because the cameras disliked dusk light as a joke
Because math is unrelated to the logs
correct_answers: Missing prints at Site B are weaker because wind can erase tracks
questions.explanation: A counter-detail weakens the competing idea.
hints: Find the sentence that says an idea fits poorly.

questions.subject: reading
questions.prompt: What should the team do next, according to the passage?
choices: Measure shell thickness and soil layers further
correct_answers: Measure shell thickness and soil layers further
questions.explanation: The closing plan is stated near the end.

questions.subject: math
questions.prompt: Dottie gathered 20 fern leaves, gave away 6, then found 9 more. How many fern leaves does Dottie have now?
hints: Do the giveaway first, then add the new find.
